text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe government, in a joint venture with two major sugar companies, Triangle Limited and Hippo Valley Estates, will build the Tokwe-Mukosi dam, set to be the country's largest inland water body, at a cost of Z$390 million.
- At least seven sections of Harare's high density suburbs were flooded on Tuesday night following a heavy rain downpour in the Zimbabwe capital.

- The Ministry of Local Government, Rural and Urban Development is investigating allegations that senior civil servants and government officials are allocating their relatives and influential friends resettlement land at the expense of more deserving people.
